title: One man's 2026 Rivalries uniform ranking: 1. Green Bay: At last, they get the white helmets correct with the yellow stripe. Bringing back the ancient interlocking "GB" logo on the jersey is brilliant. A-plus uniform. 2. Jacksonville: The jaguar spot pattern in the pants is subtle. Love the number font (especially the 7 with a dash through it; that's how I hand-write the number) and the teal helmets. The Jags now have top-shelf throwback alternates and Rivalries uniforms. They own teal in the NFL, and anything to lean into that is perfect and distinguishes them. Unfortunately, their primary uniforms with the stripe-less pants and plain jerseys are boring. 3. Chicago: Unfortunately for the Broncos, the Bears beat Denver to blue jerseys over orange pants. This shows that it works. (Of course, the Broncos could still beat the Bears by wearing orange pants in Week 3.) 4. Detroit: Quite solid, but would be better with either a) a black helmet or b) blue socks. The only primary black element is the socks. Better than going with white socks with the white pants, though; it's just that you have an unbalanced look here. A good uniform that is a tweak away from being great. 5. Houston: I wanted to like this with Columbia blue returning, but all-white is too boring for this program. The "icy white" look is akin to a low-mistake/low-risk QB. You won't look foolish, but there's nothing distinct about it; anyone can do it. A stripe pattern on the socks to match the sleeve would balance out the uniform and offer improvement. 6. Minnesota: Love the idea of the rune alphabet elements and the Nordic knot, but monochrome sinks the look. Too much purple. It's the same reason an all-orange ensemble -- helmets/jerseys/pants/socks -- wouldn't fly well for the Broncos. They'd look like pylons. Wear white pants or jerseys, and you'd have a sharp look. 7. Tennessee: Unsure how these numbers will look from a distance. Lighter-blue socks would have improved the ensemble. 8. Indianapolis: Blue socks to match the helmet would provide an upgrade. Also, royal-blue numerals on a black jersey will be difficult to discern from the upper deck, even with the white border. Fails the basic legibility test.

title: Eagles Training Camp Player Of The Day, Day 16: Tariq Woolen is really, really good at making quarterbacks pay His combination of long arms, great first step and trusting his instincts is a deadly combination that was very much on display Tuesday night Woolen’s first interception came when he had great coverage on a pass to Makai Lemon, jumping in front of Lemon to pick off the pass from Hurts. Trying to squeeze the ball past the much bigger Woolen to Lemon was a tough throw for Hurts and Woolen made him pay for attempting it. Woolen’s second interception came at the end of practice with the Eagles offense trying to drive for the win. Hurts wanted to hit Devonta Smith on the sideline but Woolen was all over it, jumping in front of the pass and taking it all the way back for a pick six (his second of camp). Woolen might be inconsistent but when he is good he is so, so good — and I could easily see him having 5+ interceptions this season

title: Jalen Hurts Training Camp Report Card, Day 16: Practicing in front of more than 45,000 fans Jalen Hurts and the Eagles offense had some extreme highs and extreme lows Let’s start with the highs Hurts had a very nice touchdown throw to Saquon Barkley from 20 yards out, throwing it over one defender into a window along the side of the end zone. The ball placement was perfect. He also had a really nice throw to Devonta Smith about 15ish yards down the field, putting it just in front of Tariq Woolen’s fingertips to Devonta who then got about another 20 yards after the catch The high point for the offense was probably a 97-yard touchdown drive (which included that pass to Devonta) which ended on a broken play to Hollywood Brown for the touchdown The lows, however, were bad Hurts had two interceptions on the night and one bad missed throw that should have been a touchdown. The missed touchdown came early in practice when Hurts had Devonta open down the middle of the field. Devonta had room but the pass was under thrown, causing Devonta to slow down and allowing Quinyon to catch up and knock it away Hurts first of two interceptions (both by Woolen) came on a pass along the sideline(ish) to Lemon. Lemon was fully covered by Woolen, who easily picked off the pass. His second interception came at the end of practice on a sideline pass to Devonta that looked to be both late and didn’t have enough on it for a sideline throw. The pass was also easily picked off and was returned for a touchdown by Woolen. Finally, Hurts had a throw on third down to Devonta that sailed out of bound, not allowing his receiver a chance to make a play on it. Overall there will be some things the Eagles like from tonight but the turnovers were bad enough to really overshadow the positive.

Jalen Hurts Training Camp Report Card, Day 16:

Practicing in front of more than 45,000 fans Jalen Hurts and the Eagles offense had some extreme highs and extreme lows

Let’s start with the highs

Hurts had a very nice touchdown throw to Saquon Barkley from 20 yards out, throwing it over one defender into a window along the side of the end zone. The ball placement was perfect. 

He also had a really nice throw to Devonta Smith about 15ish yards down the field, putting it just in front of Tariq Woolen’s fingertips to Devonta who then got about another 20 yards after the catch 

The high point for the offense was probably a 97-yard touchdown drive (which included that pass to Devonta) which ended on a broken play to Hollywood Brown for the touchdown 

The lows, however, were bad

Hurts had two interceptions on the night and one bad missed throw that should have been a touchdown. 

The missed touchdown came early in practice when Hurts had Devonta open down the middle of the field. Devonta had room but the pass was under thrown, causing Devonta to slow down and allowing Quinyon to catch up and knock it away

Hurts first of two interceptions (both by Woolen) came on a pass along the sideline(ish) to Lemon. Lemon was fully covered by Woolen, who easily picked off the pass. 

His second interception came at the end of practice on a sideline pass to Devonta that looked to be both late and didn’t have enough on it for a sideline throw. The pass was also easily picked off and was returned for a touchdown by Woolen. 

Finally, Hurts had a throw on third down to Devonta that sailed out of bound, not allowing his receiver a chance to make a play on it. 

Overall there will be some things the Eagles like from tonight but the turnovers were bad enough to really overshadow the positive.
full_text:
Jalen Hurts Training Camp Report Card, Day 16:

Practicing in front of more than 45,000 fans Jalen Hurts and the Eagles offense had some extreme highs and extreme lows

Let’s start with the highs

Hurts had a very nice touchdown throw to Saquon Barkley from 20 yards out, throwing it over one defender into a window along the side of the end zone. The ball placement was perfect. 

He also had a really nice throw to Devonta Smith about 15ish yards down the field, putting it just in front of Tariq Woolen’s fingertips to Devonta who then got about another 20 yards after the catch 

The high point for the offense was probably a 97-yard touchdown drive (which included that pass to Devonta) which ended on a broken play to Hollywood Brown for the touchdown 

The lows, however, were bad

Hurts had two interceptions on the night and one bad missed throw that should have been a touchdown. 

The missed touchdown came early in practice when Hurts had Devonta open down the middle of the field. Devonta had room but the pass was under thrown, causing Devonta to slow down and allowing Quinyon to catch up and knock it away

Hurts first of two interceptions (both by Woolen) came on a pass along the sideline(ish) to Lemon. Lemon was fully covered by Woolen, who easily picked off the pass. 

His second interception came at the end of practice on a sideline pass to Devonta that looked to be both late and didn’t have enough on it for a sideline throw. The pass was also easily picked off and was returned for a touchdown by Woolen. 

Finally, Hurts had a throw on third down to Devonta that sailed out of bound, not allowing his receiver a chance to make a play on it. 

Overall there will be some things the Eagles like from tonight but the turnovers were bad enough to really overshadow the positive.

summary:
From the media tent: CB Christian Gonzalez seems tired of answering questions about his contract status … and shares some frustration on the overall situation while highlighting the theme of focusing on Week 1.

Parts of the Q&A:

Question: How frustrating is it on your part that no contract extension has been reached?
 
Christian Gonzalez: “It’s frustrating, but I’m focused on the season. I’m focused on here now.”

- Including two players on PUP -- RB Isaac Guerendo, DL Mykel Williams -- the Niners were without a whopping 23 players in today's final full practice of training camp. 

- The new additions to the list, including a few names of guys who have missed time before today: WR Mike Evans (groin), WR Jacob Cowing (groin), G Dominick Puni (concussion), CB Upton Stout (hip flexor). Kyle Shanahan said Puni had some residual carry over from his concussion symptoms after returning to practice on Sunday. Puni will likely have to go back into the protocol. Shanahan indicated Evans, Cowing and Stout should be back to practice next week before leaving for Australia. 

- On DE Nick Bosa (tendinitis), Shanahan said he's doing well and the hope is to have him back in practice in some capacity next week as well. 

- Shanahan also said QB Kurtis Rourke (three broken ribs), G Robert Jones (calf) and OL Austen Pleasants (knee) have a shot to be back on the field next week as well. 

- Here's the full list of non participants today: 

- Bosa, Evans, Cowing, Stout, Puni, Rourke, Jones, Pleasants, DE Romello Height (ankle), LB Nick Martin (hamstring), CB Renardo Green (hamstring), LB Jalen Graham, WR Wesley Grimes (hand), DT Gracen Halton (ankle), LB Luke Gifford (hamstring), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (concussion), WR Christian Kirk (calf), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle), CB Nate Hobbs (groin)

Players on PUP: Guerendo (pec), Williams (ACL)

- Given all of that, Shanahan indicated there won't be hardly any starters playing against the Raiders on Thursday. It'll likely look similar to the Titans game as the Niners look toward the regular season. 

- TE George Kittle followed a similar blueprint as Sunday, taking part in individual drills in pads like everyone else but nothing in team periods. He did some work on the side during that but continues to look good in the drills he's doing.

- LB Dre Greenlaw took a path like Kittle's today where he didn't do much of anything in team. Niners clearly trying to get him through to the regular season. 

- That's opened up a lot of opportunities for other LBs to make an impression. One guy the Niners seem to want a longer look at given the injury situation: LB Larry Worth III. Worth got some more work today and had a nice pass breakup on a pass from QB Mac Jones for TE Jake Tonges. 

- WR De'Zhaun Stribling was in a blue no-contact jersey today and had another productive practice despite some of his defensive teammates ignoring the "no contact" part of the equation. Stribling made a great over-the-shoulder grab on a deep ball from QB Brock Purdy and held on to it with CB Jack Jones and S Marques Sigle all over him. He had another nice grab on the sideline with Jones swiping at it for a chunk of yards. A take: Stribling doesn't need to play on Thursday night. At all. 
 
- RB Christian McCaffrey's fresh legs are still evident. He had a handful of would-be explosive runs and caught a dart from Purdy over the middle that would have gone for a big gain.  

- DT Osa Odighizuwa continues to dominate inside on a regular basis. I know some will point to the Niners uncertainty at guard (especially with Puni out) and that's fair but 92 is clearly their best interior rusher and should offer a substantial upgrade over what they had last year inside. Had him down for multiple sacks and would-be pressures in team period.

- Speaking of the guys upfront, we did get another round of 1v1 pass rush today. Some notes from that... DT James Thompson Jr. does nothing but win in these. Today, he had clean wins against Nick Zakelj and Doug Kramer Jr., the latter of which was one of the most impressive reps Thompson has had in camp. I say again:  would be surprised if Thompson doesn't make the roster... Hat tip to OT Brandon Parker, who has had some struggles in this camp but strung together a few solid reps today... G Carver Willis had a rough go here today, losing decisively and quickly to DT C.J. West and DT Bryson Eason... Some good work from C Jake Brendel against West and C Drake Nugent against Evan Anderson and Eason. Growing more intrigued with Nugent as the possible backup C the closer we get to the cut to 53, especially with Toth still out. 

- Sigle had an interception on a pass from Purdy for WR Demarcus Robinson. The throw was a little high, tipped off Robinson's hands and Sigle made a nice play on it for the pick. 

- Purdy otherwise had another solid day, finding TE Luke Farrell for a couple of touchdowns in the red zone, completing what looked like a no look pass to WR KhaDarel Hodge and dropping one in to McCaffrey over LB Fred Warner and in front of LB Jaden Dugger for a big gain.

- Some more defensive highlights: Deommodore Lenoir got to move around a bit more today and had a nice PBU early against Farrell... Had DE Sam Okuayinonu and DE Keion White down for would-be sacks/pressures... LB Garret Wallow, who also got some extra ops with Greenlaw not in team, had a PBU against Tonges... Dugger got his hand on a ball that nearly went for a big completion to Stribling but Dugger got enough of it to force the incompletion. 

- The Niners have a walkthrough on Wednesday, game Thursday and then the weekend off to trim the roster to 53 by Sunday. The decisions won't be easy and so much will depend on injuries. Could be a lot of juggling with vested veterans being released and brought back so others can go to IR, etc. 

-- Names we're watching here as guys who could be involved in some of that juggling: Kirk, Lowe, Jones, Hobbs, Martin, Toth. Also, wouldn't be surprised to see Williams and Guerendo remain on PUP. With new rules allowing them to come back to practice as soon as Week 3, it would just make sense. 

- Obviously, plenty more to come this season but that'll do it for these long practice reports for this season. Appreciate all of you who took the time to read even parts of them. Thanks and have a good Tuesday.

title: Right before one of the final team periods, the offense and defense huddled up, which was a decision made by cornerback Jaylon Johnson to bring the team together, according to Cole Kmet. Johnson's message to the team? "It's not good enough," according to safety Cam Lewis. We haven't seen the full team gather like that during a practice unless it's 'all up' at the end, which is called by Ben Johnson. It was a move made by a veteran team leader that helped the Bears finish off what Kmet said was one of their best practices of camp. Another example of Johnson's leadership on display today was when he helped Montez Sweat back to the defense's sideline after the long-drive drill. Understandably exhausted, Sweat was closest to the offense's sideline so he took a knee there after the drive ended. Johnson walked over, helped him up and jogged with him back to the defense's sideline.

The pecking order there seems like Newsome-Banks-Adebo-Hood. • There is still some rotating at safety, but it seems like Tyler Nubin is gaining a stronger hold on the starting spot next to Jevon Holland. • Lucas Patrick and Bryan Hudson rotated at center with the second-team. One of the position battles that still seems undecided.

• There is still some rotating at safety, but it seems like Tyler Nubin is gaining a stronger hold on the starting spot next to Jevon Holland.

title: Bears Practice 17 (Padded 9) in the books ... The day's biggest story is Darnell Wright's exit from practice with an apparent right arm injury. With all the instability at left tackle, the Bears don't need to be in troubleshooting mode on the right side also. Offensively, Bears 1s were out of sync during a 7-on-7 period where the ball found the grass on five of six Caleb Williams passes. Dayo Odeyingbo with a couple flashes of disruption today, including a pass batted down in the backfield. If replay review were a thing in camp, it might have been ruled a lateral and a 50-yard Dayo scoop and score. Caleb's prettiest throw was a scramble drill deep shot (with plenty of air and touch) to Colston Loveland on a completion that probably went for 55+. (Context footnote: Williams was likely sacked on the play by Devin Bush) Rome Odunze with another in-traffic, strong hands grab of a Williams dart over the middle on a third-down play. Practice ended with a long drive drill. Players on both sides of the ball were gassed.

I didn’t see what happened, but the reaction from teammates was telling. All of the WRs and DBs couldn’t even look as trainers attended to Austin. The rest of the team was at the other end of the field doing a 9-on-7 drill. The whole team came down to wish Austin well before he was carted off. The WRs and DBs did a lengthy prayer circle until practice resumed. Sometimes things don’t turn out as bad as the initial reactions, but this one definitely looked very bad.

title: AFC Team-By-Team Thoughts Ravens – Ja’Kobi Lane hype worth taking seriously w/ Rashod Bateman situation. Bills – Dalton Kincaid my favorite TE breakout pick in ’26. Bengals – Condensed juggernaut offense + improved OL insulates floor & ceiling for every Cincy skill player. Browns – Betting Shedeur Sanders starts Browns home opener (Week 3 vs. Carolina). Broncos – I think Jonah Coleman is next man up if J.K. Dobbins goes down, which he typically does. Texans – Kayshon Boutte helps Nico Collins. Low-target % deep threat can clear space vertically. Jaguars – Parker Washington is Jags only skill player I’m actively pursuing in drafts at this point. Chiefs – Kenneth Walker my longshot bet for Offensive Player of Year. Raiders – Tre Tucker has separated as Raiders No. 1 WR, draft worthy in all leagues. Chargers – Keaton Mitchell “setback” top storyline worth monitoring at Bolts camp. Dolphins – Should shop stud C Aaron Brewer to Chargers, who lost Tyler Biadasz. Mike McDaniel connection. Patriots – Bumped up Romeo Doubs after Kayshon Boutte trade. Becomes clear No. 2 WR behind 29yo No. 1 with health/performance flags. Jets – Drafters of Jets players need Geno Smith to survive. No margin for error. Next up at QB: 4th-round rookie Cade Klubnik. Steelers – Can envision Pat Freiermuth as one of hottest post-Week 1 pickups at TE. Titans – Buried Carnell Tate in WR Rankings. Faith in Cam Ward evaporating behind league-worst OL. Wan ‘Dale Robinson only Titans WR to target.

title: Steel Magnolias will always be my favorite Dolly movie. Truvy was everything 🥹 The fact this icon got in a cheerleaders hot pants and performed at Thanksgiving will forever be a moment I’m glad I got to see in person. She personified “bless your heart” by putting men in the industry in their place with a sassy little line and a smile and owned who she was with her trademark humor and southern charm. She gave to so many and fiercely loved and protected her man. She was special and I always got a kick out of folks saying I looked like younger Dolly. I should be so lucky. 🥲

title: NFC Team-By-Team Thoughts Cardinals – Trey Benson cut. James Conner hurt. Tyler Allgeier Week 1 flex starter if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) doesn’t play. Falcons – Michael Penix’s timeline to start keeps feeling closer. Week 1 even in play. Panthers – Chuba Hubbard-Jonathon Brooks wars will probably yield no true victor due to bad QB/OL & committee approach that won’t go away. Bears – Buying everyone. Offensive juggernaut + swinging-gate defense. Cowboys – Javonte Williams beneficiary of unsettled backfield behind him. Javonte should have one of highest RB usage rates. Lions – See Bears, but in a dome. Packers – MarShawn Lloyd my most-drafted RB in best ball. Rams – Several concerns RE: offensive efficiency repeat: OL, aging at most critical spots, regression for 2025’s outrageous rate stats. Vikings – Justin Jefferson my scariest 2026 “fade.” (I’m dead even with his WR6 positional ADP but a few slots below in overall rankings and therefore never get him in drafts.) Saints – Juwan Johnson most undervalued FF tight end coming off 77/889/3 season with Jordyn Tyson out indefinitely. Giants – Najee Harris’ skill set overlaps with Cam Skattebo; 220+ lb, 4.6 types, pass-game functional. (Both off severe injury, too.) Interchangeable. Eagles – Makai Lemon (hamstring) finally practicing. ADP has fallen far enough to draft him as priority bench stash. 49ers – Sounds like third-round rookie Kaelon Black is preferred RB stash behind CMC, who’s coming off career high in touches. Seahawks – Rave reviews for Jadarian Price but looming return of Zach Charbonnet quiets upside. Seahawks obsessed with Charbonnet on pass downs, near GL. Bucs – Chris Godwin (affordable in drafts) arguably most stable Bucs pass catcher with Emeka Egbuka battling toe injury, Ted Hurst pushing Jalen McMillan. Commanders – Preseason signs point to Chig Okonkwo as true every-down TE. Quietly has 50+ catches in 3 straight seasons. Should be his career year.

I haven't seen it yet, but someone told me he was mic'ed up in that first game and he's coming to the sideline, he's talking to Grady about the things that are happening on the field. Grady's helping him, giving him tidbits here and there. It's a good thing to see right now. He's firmly in the mix."
